column6: Worked the five-column trace; majority and up-to-date checks are sound.
Earlier-term commit rule, up-to-date comparison, crash-only model and liveness role of timeouts all match the Raft paper.
Called the up-to-date voting check the "election safety property"; in Raft, Election Safety means at most one leader per term. Renamed to "election restriction".
Same mislabel ("election safety condition"); renamed to "election restriction".
Worked the lagging-replica scenario and the three fixes; second-device prompt is apt.
Worked the placement-by-failure grid; quorum-of-2 outcomes and slowest-link column come out as intended.
Bullet 2 said "the data is safe" after losing the home region; the remote replica need not be in any write quorum, so it may lack recent acknowledged writes. Replaced with that caveat.
With only "minimize write latency" as the goal, option C (one datacenter) beats keyed answer B. Added the disaster-recovery requirement so B is the right answer.
At least 2 cross-region round trips: acks arrive in parallel, so the floor is one cross-region round trip (matches Q4 answer).
Statement "typically reduces read latency" was true, yet keyed false (its own explanation agreed reads get faster). Reworded to "reduces both read and write latency" so false is correct.
Enumerated all 6 interleavings: outcomes (0,1), (1,0), (1,1); (0,0) never appears and requires a cycle, as stated.

Said SC is achievable with "causal ordering or vector clocks"; those give causal consistency, not a single total order. Removed the example. Also note (not fixed): Explainer claims SC has "higher availability" than linearizability, which is doubtful (SC is not available under partition either).
Worked the log: in order x=2; swapped last two gives x=3; clock example is apt.
Note: new snapshot bullet makes old q:1 option B (take a snapshot) partly defensible; key (log replay) still holds, left as is.
Worked the G-counter: merge gives [2,3,1] = 6 in any order and with duplicates; summing totals inflates on duplicate.

Keyed option said replicas "may converge to different states" under eventual consistency, which contradicts EC's own convergence promise. Reworded to "may be in different states after applying the same updates".
Said "incrementing twice ... gives the same result as once (idempotent)"; increments are not idempotent, state merges are. Reworded to merging the same state twice.
Said text-editing CRDTs use "techniques from the operational transformation family"; OT is a separate approach. Replaced with "sequence CRDTs such as RGA".
Worked the 3-second silence under each model; conclusions are correct.
FLP bullet dropped the qualifier that at least one process may crash (without faults, asynchronous consensus is solvable). Added it.
Worked the state diagram and three crash points with the termination rule; all outcomes consistent. Note (not fixed): Core Idea's "releasing read locks" at pre-commit is not a standard part of 3PC.

Exercise failed when worked: with 1-second buckets and a 1-second first delay, full jitter still puts all 100 retries in one bucket, so its peak matches plain backoff. Changed delays to 5, 10, 20 s, so jitter spreads about 20 per second, matching capacity.
3 layers x 3 attempts = 27 checks out.
Enumerated the 4 three-replica quorums from R2-R5; each contains R2 or R3.
Bullet 3 said "a majority quorum is enough" without qualification; the file also covers PBFT, which needs 2f+1 of 3f+1. Scoped the majority argument to crash-tolerant protocols.
